When two providers serve the same model with different prices, the engine picks by name or score, not cost.\n\n## Scope\n\n### Data model\n\nAdd to `internal/routing.ProviderEntry`:\n\n- `CostUSDPer1kTokens float64` — nil/zero if unknown.\n- `CostSource string` — `\"catalog\" | \"subscription\" | \"unknown\" | \"user-config\"`. When the catalog has a price, use it. When absent, leave zero + `CostSource: \"unknown\"`.\n- **Subscription harnesses (claude, codex, gemini):** compute an **effective** cost as a function of quota utilization:\n  - At 0-70% quota used: effective cost = 0 (fixed-cost subscription, near-zero marginal).\n  - At 70-90%: effective cost = low (encourage spreading load).\n  - At 90-100%: effective cost = high (near-quota demotion).\n  - Exact numbers in the bead acceptance; tunable via `ServiceOptions`.\n  - `CostSource: \"subscription\"`.\n- **`agent` harness (local via endpoints):** cost = electricity estimate from config (off by default — `CostSource: \"unknown\"` when not configured). Operators who want to model local cost set `ServiceOptions.LocalCostUSDPer1kTokens`.\n\n### Scoring changes\n\n`internal/routing/score.go`: add cost as a tiebreak dimension **after** eligibility, quota OK, and base score. Order becomes:\n1. Eligible\n2. Quota OK / healthy\n3. Base score (profile policy, cooldowns, perf bias) — unchanged\n4. **Cost (lower is better)** — new\n5. Locality (local cost-class preferred)\n6. Name\n\nFor unknown-cost providers (`CostSource: \"unknown\"`): treat as **neutral** in the cost tiebreak — neither preferred nor demoted, so they don't starve known-cost providers but aren't penalized into last place.\n\n### Unknown-cost policy\n\nA documented rule: when all viable candidates have `CostSource: \"unknown\"`, the cost tiebreak is skipped and locality/name decide. Consumer migration note published.","claimed-at":"2026-04-20T03:59:51Z","claimed-machine":"eitri","claimed-pid":"994875","created_at":"2026-04-20T03:48:09.234052812Z","description":"Surfaced while migrating ddx (consumer) from ddx-agent v0.5.0 → v0.6.0 (see DDx tracker ddx-4535f466; sibling agent bead agent-117a0868).\n\n## Argument\n\nv0.6.0 added `ProviderPreference` (`LocalFirst` / `SubscriptionFirst` / `LocalOnly` / `SubscriptionOnly`) to `RouteRequest` as the consumer-facing placement knob. This sits in an uncanny valley:\n\n- It's **too abstract to be a real choice** — a caller who cares enough about placement to set it usually has more specific intent (\"only local because I'm offline\", \"cloud because this one task is worth $2\", \"openrouter-haiku for this batch because I know the shape\"). The 4-value enum can't express any of that.\n\n- It's **too specific to delegate** — a caller who doesn't want to think about placement shouldn't have to pick one of four values at every call site. The right default depends on tier, cost budget, connectivity, and user policy — none of which `ProviderPreference` sees.\n\n- Every consumer that plumbs it through ends up re-deriving the same tier→preference translation (cheap → LocalFirst, smart → SubscriptionFirst), which is (a) duplicated across consumers, (b) guaranteed to drift, and (c) not tunable without a code change.\n\n## The richer abstraction that already almost exists: profiles\n\nA profile is a named bundle of multi-axis policy. Examples of what profiles can express that `ProviderPreference` can't:\n\n- `cheap`: prefer local; fall back to openrouter-haiku; never opus; stall-kill aggressively; cap reasoning at 2k tokens\n- `offline`: local-only; fail loud if no local provider; no network calls at all\n- `smart-but-cheap`: subscription-first but only models under $5/Mtok input\n- `air-gapped`: local-only + disable telemetry + reject any http provider\n- `code-high`: any provider, coding-tuned models, reasoning=high, prefer large context\n\n`ProviderPreference` reduces all of that to one axis. A profile is a data structure, and data structures compose.\n\nv0.6.0's `models.yaml` already has `surface_policy` per target carrying `effort_default` and `reasoning_default`. Extending that to carry placement order, cost ceilings, and failure policy is an additive change; the shape is already there.\n\n## Proposal\n\n1. **Remove `RouteRequest.ProviderPreference`** from the public service surface (v0.7.0 breaking change; acceptable now because adoption is low and we're already mid-migration).\n2. **Reinstate profiles as the consumer-facing routing knob.** `RouteRequest.Profile` (or let `ModelRef` carry a profile name — today `ModelRef` already accepts tier names like `cheap`/`standard`/`smart`, so this may be a simple semantic consolidation, not a new field).\n3. **Move placement policy into profile/catalog definitions.** Each profile/target declares its own candidate providers, candidate models, placement order, reasoning defaults, cost ceilings, and failure policy. Users retune by editing one file (`models.yaml` or user override).\n4. **Pinpoint control stays as an escape hatch.** Callers that already know the exact provider + model pass `Provider` + `Model` directly and bypass the profile machinery entirely. That's the \"if I'm going to micromanage I'll just set the provider\" path — preserved, not denied.\n5. **No per-call-site policy expression.** Consumers that don't know placement don't have to decide it. The profile does.\n\n## Why this matters for the consumer side\n\nDDx's ddx-4535f466 Track B was originally \"audit every `ResolveRoute` call site and add the right `ProviderPreference`.\" If this proposal lands, that track collapses to zero: callers either use a profile (and the agent decides placement) or pin Provider+Model (and they own placement). No middle layer for DDx to translate.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n1. `RouteRequest.ProviderPreference` removed from the public surface; `ProviderPreference` constants no longer exported.\n2. Profiles (named, multi-axis policy bundles) are the documented public routing knob. CONTRACT-003 updated.\n3. `surface_policy` in `models.yaml` carries placement order + cost ceilings + failure policy, not just reasoning defaults.\n4. A consumer wanting \"local-first cheap\" sets `Profile: \"cheap\"` and the catalog's cheap profile expresses \"prefer local, fall back to openrouter-haiku\". A consumer wanting pinpoint control sets `Provider` + `Model` and bypasses the profile machinery.\n5. Migration note in CHANGELOG for any v0.6.0 consumer that started using `ProviderPreference`.","execute-loop-heartbeat-at":"2026-04-20T03:59:51.212118813Z","id":"agent-285a05d2","issue_type":"task","labels":["area:service","area:routing","area:catalog","kind:design","phase:design"],"owner":"erik","priority":1,"status":"closed","title":"RouteRequest.ProviderPreference is the uncanny valley — reinstate profiles as the public routing knob","updated_at":"2026-04-20T04:03:32.072580045Z"}

Must **never** return gemini.
